## Other tools that connect these apps and where Activepieces fits


Zapier and Make are hosted tools that bill by usage, Calendly's native Salesforce option is built in, and Activepieces lets you run the flow on your own server, with an MIT-licensed core and 750 integrations to draw on, so you can connect to The text came through as a fragment ("most services you're already using."), with no competitor, numbers, product names, or superlative to remove.

### Comparing options by integration step costs


Your booking flow isn't one step. A sound one searches Salesforce for an existing contact, creates or updates it, then logs the meeting, and every extra step is where a metered tool starts charging you.


The table shows how the four options differ on the things that decide that. Read the cost and step columns together, because a cheap plan with a tight meter isn't cheap for a flow with a lookup in it.


Option Cost model Hosting Step limits Control


Activepieces Free to self-host as open source Your server, or their hosted version Unlimited steps per the docs High: you own the runtime and the flow


Zapier Per task; Professional is $19.99 for 750 tasks Zapier's cloud Each action step counts against the task allowance Medium: configure in their editor


Make Per operation; Core is $16 Make's cloud Each module run counts as an operation Medium-high: visual branching and routing


Native Calendly-Salesforce option Part of the Calendly side, no separate tool Calendly's side Nothing to count, but nothing to add Low: fixed fields and fixed behavior


> a cheap plan with a tight meter isn't cheap for a flow with a lookup in it.


At 750 tasks, a three-action booking flow covers roughly 250 bookings before you hit the ceiling.


Make's $16 is the lower entry price, but you pay in operations, so a flow with branches uses its allowance faster than it looks.


The native option has no meter at all, and its price is that you take the mapping it ships with.


### When unlimited steps and data privacy matter


Choose it when the flow needs more steps than you want to pay for, or when booking data shouldn't pass through another vendor's cloud.


The docs say steps are unlimited, so the lookup-before-create step that prevents duplicate contacts costs you nothing extra. That matters because duplicates are the most common matching failure in this pairing.


You also decide who can see the Salesforce credentials if you self-host, which is the permission mistake the article warned about earlier.


You pay for that by running it. If nobody on your team wants to maintain a server, the hosted version removes that burden, and Zapier or Make may still be the calmer choice.


Pick one tool and build one flow: a new Calendly booking that finds the contact in Salesforce, updates it if it exists and creates it if not.


Book a test meeting with an address already in Salesforce and a second with a brand-new one. If the first makes a duplicate, fix the match before adding a single new step.
